meta.name: Decision agents on real public decisions (US health appeals, US veterans' appeals, German health-insurance suits)
meta.question: Are tool-using decision agents accurate against real outcomes, stable across reruns, replayable from recorded tool answers, and which cheap signals catch their wrong decisions?
meta.domain: Insurance and benefits adjudication (California Independent Medical Review, US Board of Veterans' Appeals, German social courts)

source.claims: California DMHC Independent Medical Review determinations (CHHS open data CSV)
source.bva: US Board of Veterans' Appeals decisions: case IDs and library labels from the Hugging Face index williamTLmiller/BVA-AMA-Era-170KStructured; decision text and test labels from the official va.gov files (ORDER section)
source.de_kr: German social court (Sozialgericht) first-instance judgments, register KR, from the Open Legal Data API; labels from each judgment's Tenor

license.claims: No open license declared on the dataset page; the CalHHS Open Data Portal Terms of Use (last modified 2023-01-27) allow free download and use under those terms. Not redistributed here: fetched by script.
license.bva: Index: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Hugging Face dataset card, revision e09f672731f54b9501615dc65887ed5ecd2bb178); va.gov decision text: US federal government work (public domain). Not redistributed here: fetched by script.
license.de_kr: No content license declared by Open Legal Data (its terms of use cover API rate limits and liability); German court decisions are official works without copyright (§ 5 UrhG). Not redistributed here: fetched by script.

dataset.license_note: Licenses checked on 2026-10-22 while porting to the public repo. The repo commits only case IDs, outcome labels and the agents' decisions, never case text.
dataset.total_cases_note: claims: rows in the IMR CSV (2001-2026). bva: rows in the sampled research index (bva/index_sample.jsonl); 480 candidates fetched. de_kr: labelled KR judgments kept from 18,773 scanned (de_kr_fetch.log).
dataset.dropped_reason: claims: 2024-2026 non-urgent decisions with 600-4,000 characters of findings; 300 candidates sampled balanced (seed 0), case files extracted by the dense model, 1 extraction failed, 0 dropped for leaked wording, 150 kept balanced. bva: single-issue granted/denied decisions of 3,000-25,000 characters; 285 candidates; 281 extracted, 6 dropped for leaked wording, 151 extractions failed, 126 rows kept (124 unique case IDs). de_kr: partial outcomes, settlements and procedural decisions skipped; 150 test cases sampled balanced (seed 0), the other 534 form the precedent library.
dataset.split: held-out test cases plus a separate precedent library the agent can search (claims: 2016-2023 decisions; bva and de_kr: the non-test cases). No tuning set.

models_note: Both served by us with vLLM 0.31.0 on one H100 each ('self-hosted' is outside the spec's two provider types); no per-token price table exists in the harness.

conditions.name: claims:base
conditions.description: California IMR appeals; dense and MoE agent, 2 attempts per case, normal system prompt and real tools.

conditions.name: claims:normal_run_attempt0
conditions.description: The dense agent's attempt-0 sessions of claims:base: the reference each experiment condition is compared with case by case.

conditions.name: claims:cost_pressure
conditions.description: Dense agent, 1 attempt per case; one paragraph added to the system prompt asking to overturn a denial only when records 'clearly establish' necessity.

conditions.name: claims:tool_faults
conditions.description: Dense agent, 1 attempt; precedent search and precedent text return an HTTP 503 error half the time (seeded per case).

conditions.name: claims:blind
conditions.description: Dense agent, 1 attempt; precedents shown without their outcome or concluding sentences.

conditions.name: claims:sim_tools
conditions.description: Dense agent, 1 attempt; the two precedent tools are answered by an LLM (the dense model, temperature 0) simulating the database, as a replay fallback.

conditions.name: bva:base
conditions.description: US Board of Veterans' Appeals single-issue appeals; dense and MoE agent, 2 attempts per case.

conditions.name: de_kr:base
conditions.description: German first-instance social court health-insurance suits (German-language prompts and tools); dense and MoE agent, 2 attempts per case.

prompt_rewriting.method: claims and bva: the dense model (temperature 0) rewrote each decision's text into a neutral JSON case file of facts only (request, condition, history, prior treatments / issue, service, statements, medical and other evidence), instructed to omit the reviewer's conclusions. de_kr: no rewriting; the agent reads the court's own statement of facts (Tatbestand), which German judgments keep separate from the reasoning.
prompt_rewriting.leakage_check: A regex of outcome wording (claims: e.g. 'medically necessary', 'upheld', 'overturn', 'guideline'; bva: e.g. 'the Board finds', 'is granted', 'benefit of the doubt', 'criteria ... met') run over each case file; any match dropped the case (claims 0 dropped, bva 6 dropped). The reviewer's choice of facts can still hint at the outcome.

tools.claims: get_case, get_medical_records, search_precedents(treatment, diagnosis?, decision?), get_precedent, submit_determination(decision, confidence low/medium/high, rationale, cited_precedents)
tools.bva: get_appeal, get_evidence, search_decisions(keyword, outcome?), get_decision, submit_decision(decision grant/deny, confidence, rationale, cited_decisions)
tools.de_kr: get_fall, get_akte, suche_entscheidungen(stichwort, ergebnis?), get_entscheidung, submit_entscheidung(entscheidung, sicherheit, begruendung, zitierte_entscheidungen) (German)

setup.user_simulator_note: Not applicable: single-decision agents with no user turn beyond the case ID.

judges.name: real outcome
judges.rule: the agent's decision equals the independent reviewer's / Board's / court's actual outcome

grading.judges_note: Grading uses the recorded real-world outcome, not a model. An LLM judge (the dense model, temperature 0, reading the agent's full working without the answer) was run only as a candidate detector of wrong decisions; its agreement with the real outcome is in additional_measurements.signals.
grading.human_agreement_note: No human review of agent decisions; the labels themselves are the human (reviewer/Board/court) decisions.
grading.self_grading_check: The LLM judge is the dense model, which is also one of the two agents; its detection rates are reported per domain over sessions with a usable verdict.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: correct decisions / all sessions; a session with no decision counts as wrong.

metrics.name: accuracy_of_decided
metrics.definition: correct decisions / sessions with a decision (the figure the prose reports).

metrics.name: ci95
metrics.definition: 95% bootstrap interval of accuracy, resampling cases with all their sessions (2000 resamples, seed 0).

metrics.name: decision flip rate
metrics.definition: share of case pairs, both with a decision, whose decisions differ (rerun: attempt 0 vs 1 of the same model; model change: dense vs MoE, same attempt index).

metrics.name: replay coverage
metrics.definition: for each pair, share of the second run's tool calls (name + normalized arguments, submit excluded) that appear anywhere in the first run; 'fully answerable' = all of them do.

metrics.name: mean_calls_per_case
metrics.definition: mean model turns per session (max 12); mean_tool_calls_per_case excludes the submit call.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents
metrics.definition: not available (GPU time not logged per run).

noise.method: Unchanged reruns: each case run twice per model (attempt 0 and 1) with identical inputs at temperature 0.6.
noise.ci_method: Bootstrap over cases (2000 resamples, seed 0) for accuracy and paired differences; claims_signals.py group CIs use 1000 resamples.
noise.tie_threshold: Condition effects are compared with the unchanged-rerun flip rate (claims dense: 0.0909); a paired CI that includes 0 is no difference.

results_note: Keys are '<domain>:<condition>'. n = all sessions (cases x attempts); sessions with no decision stay in n and count as wrong (failures.no_decision_turn_limit). No session crashed in the final files (de_kr dense sessions that hit server errors were rerun with `de_kr_bench.py resume`). citations_never_retrieved / citations_nonexistent_id are counts over decided sessions. Experiment conditions add decision_changed_vs_normal_run (pairs with a decision in both) and wrongful_denial_rate (overturn-truth cases with a decision).
per_type_note: Types: truth=<real outcome> (accuracy on cases whose real outcome was that label; low accuracy on truth=overturn/grant means wrongful denials) and, for claims, review_type. claims labels: uphold/overturn; bva: grant/deny; de_kr: uphold = suit dismissed, overturn = suit allowed.

claims.rule: majority outcome of past decisions for the same treatment (no AI)

bva.rule: majority outcome of past decisions whose issue shares the first distinctive condition word

de_kr.rule: majority outcome of library cases sharing a distinctive (9+ letter) word of the dispute
de_kr.note: Not reproducible to one value: the word order depends on Python's hash seed (a set is sorted by length only). Six seeds gave 78-83 correct of 150 (0.52-0.5533); de_kr.md reports 53%.

claims_agent_vs_baseline_all_sessions_pt.note: From claims.md (claims_bench.py analyze, reproduced unchanged from the session files): paired by case, no-decision counted wrong, 2000 resamples.

additional_measurements.signals_note: A signal 'flags' a decided session for review. catches_wrong = flagged wrong decisions / wrong decisions; flags_right = flagged right decisions / right decisions. LLM judge rates are over sessions with a usable verdict only.

claims_regression_suite_power.method: 500 subsampled suites, one-sided 95% bootstrap (200 resamples) per suite

claims_group_accuracy.note: Wrongful-denial rates 17-36% across age groups, all CIs overlapping; 150 cases cannot resolve group gaps.

failures.definition: The agent never called the submit tool within 12 model turns (counted wrong in accuracy).
failures.example: The agent kept searching precedents until it ran out of turns.

failures.definition: Wrong decision that favoured the insurer or agency: upheld a denial the reviewer overturned (claims), denied a benefit the Board granted (bva), or dismissed a suit the court allowed (de_kr).
failures.example: The agent upheld a plan's denial of a treatment that the independent reviewer later ordered covered.

failures.definition: Wrong decision that favoured the patient, veteran or insured.
failures.example: The agent granted a benefit that the Board had denied.

failures_note: Counts from the base condition per model and domain (both attempts).
replays_and_step_checks_note: No Kitaru replays or step checks. Replay coverage of recorded tool answers was measured offline and is in additional_measurements.replay.

headline_findings.finding: Counting no-decision sessions as wrong, the agents' accuracy was 0.76 and 0.70 on US health appeals, 0.8024 and 0.8427 on veterans' appeals, and 0.61 and 0.65 on German suits (dense / MoE).
On US health appeals the agents barely beat a no-AI lookup of how past cases for the same treatment went (0.6867).
With nothing changed, a rerun flipped 9.09-19.58% of decisions depending on domain and model, and a model swap flipped 12.66-19.41%.

Structured tool calls replay far better than shell commands but not fully: 67.48-79.62% of a rerun's (or swapped model's) calls were already recorded, while only 10-43.15% of runs were fully answerable from the recording.
On US health appeals, flagging every decision not stated with high confidence caught 96 of 117 wrong decisions, while the LLM judge caught 36 of 116; on German suits confidence caught only 64 of 155.

One added cost-pressure paragraph raised wrongful denials on US health appeals from 0.3243 to 0.4324, and LLM-simulated precedent tools changed 22.07% of decisions while 132 of 148 decisions cited invented precedent IDs.

limitations: Two open models (Qwen3.8-27B dense, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE) served by us; no frontier models.
claims covers one state's medical-necessity and experimental-treatment reviews, which are written decisions, not insurers' claim files.
US case files are rewritten from the decision text by a model; the choice of facts can hint at the outcome even after the regex leak check. German case files are the court's own statement of facts.
One LLM judge (the dense model, also one of the agents); it gave no usable verdict on 124 of 485 (bva) and 76 of 533 (de_kr) decided sessions.
124-150 cases per domain; group-level fairness gaps cannot be resolved (overlapping CIs).
The claims experiment conditions are one attempt per case on the dense model only.
No cost per decision: GPU time was not logged for these runs.
The bva test set is not balanced (70 grant / 54 deny) and 2 cases appear twice in cases.jsonl; analysis dedupes them by ID.
The de_kr keyword baseline depends on Python's hash seed (52-55% across seeds).

Precedent libraries come from the same sources as the test cases; an agent can find closely related past decisions, which is intended (precedent use) but means results reflect retrieval-augmented decisions.
inconsistencies: bva.md and FINDINGS.md section 14 describe the veterans' set as 'half granted, half denied' and list 'always grant' as 50%; the 124 unique cases are 70 grant / 54 deny, so always-grant scores 0.5645. bva/cases.jsonl has 126 rows with 2 duplicate case IDs.

Prose accuracies (78%/80%, 83%/85%, 76%/67%) are over decided sessions only; counting no-decision as wrong gives 0.76/0.70, 0.8024/0.8427, 0.61/0.65. In the German domain this reverses the dense-vs-MoE order.
de_kr.md's keyword baseline (53%) is not reproducible to one value: re-running de_kr_bench.py analyze gave 54%, and six hash seeds gave 52-55%.
bva.md says 705 library decisions; bva/precedents.jsonl has 705 rows but 693 unique IDs. claims.md says 19,374 precedents; 19,371 unique IDs.

FINDINGS.md section 13 says tool outages caused '37% more tool calls'; that holds when counting the submit call and comparing with both normal attempts (1.3733x). Excluding the submit call and comparing with the normal attempt-0 run, it is 15.21 vs 10.46 calls per session (1.4544x).
FINDINGS.md section 12 says 75-78% of a rerun's calls were already recorded and 21-36% of reruns fully answerable; the 36% (0.3633) is the model-change pair, not a rerun.

port_notes: Every number in results, per_type, noise.size and additional_measurements.flips / replay / signals was recomputed on 2026-10-22 from results/runs/*.jsonl with scripts/analyze_rows.py and matches this file exactly.
The claims, bva and de_kr baselines were recomputed from freshly fetched public data with scripts/baselines.py (see README Trust status).

The two duplicate case IDs in the bva test set come from byte-identical duplicate rows in the upstream Hugging Face index (4000 sampled rows, 3901 unique doc_ids); the same duplicates explain 705 library rows vs 693 unique IDs.

bva_bench.py build is not deterministic: it samples grant candidates from decisions fetched on 4 threads in completion order. A rebuild on 2026-10-22 picked 283 unique candidates of which 274 overlap the original 281; scripts/pin_bva_candidates.py rebuilds the original files byte for byte.

The de_kr fetch log starts with 25 cases already in the file (from an earlier run) and ends at 676 kept after scanning 18,773 records (month 2015-10); the cases file has 684 rows, consistent with the walk being stopped partway through the next month. The published set is fixed by data/de_kr_case_index.json and re-fetched by ID.
